title: RAG Authoring Cheatsheet + WASM Adapter Scenario Sandbox
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: New quickstart: compact RAG authoring cheatsheet with a local WASM adapter sandbox, stepwise assertion templates, and telemetry presets for scenario-driven debugging. No breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for a minimal, device-friendly authoring workflow that demonstrates writing RAG step assertions and debugging tool-calls locally without a heavy infra dependency. This PR introduces a compact cheatsheet for RAG authoring and a small WASM adapter scenario sandbox that runs in the browser or node-wasm runner to exercise tool-calling and step assertions deterministically. Goals: 1) provide a one-page cheatsheet for prompt/step design and failure modes, 2) include a runnable sandbox that can simulate tool responses (WASM + JSON fixtures) so authors can iterate locally, 3) wire lightweight telemetry presets to produce deterministic traces for QA and evals, and 4) add a smoke CI job so the quickstart remains runnable in CI.

What changed (single-string summary): Added docs/cheatsheets/rag-authoring-cheatsheet.md, quickstarts/wasm-sandbox/README.md, quickstarts/wasm-sandbox/adapter.wasm (small adapter stub), quickstarts/wasm-sandbox/fixtures/*.json, quickstarts/wasm-sandbox/playwright/smoke.spec.ts, examples/rag-step-assertions/sample.prompts, tooling/ci/quickstart-smoke.yml, and small updates to docs/site-sidebars.json to surface the cheatsheet.

Commits (high-level): 1) init: add cheatsheet and README with examples and step assertions, 2) wasm: add compiled adapter stub and fixture harness, 3) tests: add playwright smoke test and node-runner glue, 4) docs: hook cheatsheet into sidebars and add cross-links to telemetry presets, 5) ci: add quickstart-smoke workflow and fix lint issues from review.

Files of interest (illustrative): - docs/cheatsheets/rag-authoring-cheatsheet.md: compact rules, example sequence diagrams, failure-mode checklist and recommended telemetry probes (trace anchors and step IDs). - quickstarts/wasm-sandbox/README.md: local-run instructions for both browser preview and node-wasm runner, how to seed fixtures and assert steps. - quickstarts/wasm-sandbox/playwright/smoke.spec.ts: an end-to-end sanity runner that loads the wasm adapter, replays a fixture, and asserts final structured output. - examples/rag-step-assertions/sample.prompts: minimal set of prompt templates used by the cheatsheet.

Review conversation (highlights): Liam O'Connor: "Nice compact format, shippedable for first-time authors. Two minor nitpicks: 1) make telemetry anchors optional by default, 2) add an example showing tool-call fallback behavior." Priya Shah (author): "Addressed both: telemetry anchors guarded behind TELEMETRY=1 flag and added a fallback example in sample.prompts (commit 3)." Avery Kim: "Playwright smoke is flaky when run in parallel on small runners — can we pin to --retries=1 in workflow?" Priya Shah: "Updated quickstart-smoke.yml to run sequentially and added a comment explaining resource assumptions (commit 5)." Diego Martinez: "Docs cross-links look good; suggest adding a brief paragraph on how this ties into the Optimize recommendations." Priya Shah: "Added OPTIMIZE note and a link to ENG-1429 in the cheatsheet."

CI summary: quickstart-smoke workflow (node 20 + playwright) — passed on run #3 after rerunning flaky browser boot step; lint/job checks passed (prettier/markdownlint), unit tests for node-runner passed, smoke run completed in ~45s. Coverage not applicable for wasm stub.

Security and compliance: WASM adapter is a tiny stub with no external network access by default; README documents how to enable outbound connector stubbing and KMS usage for private keys. No secrets checked in.

How to use (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/wasm-sandbox; 2) npm ci && npm run start:preview to open browser sandbox; 3) TELEMETRY=1 npm run replay -- --fixture=happy-path.json to collect trace anchors locally; 4) run playwright smoke locally with npm run smoke. The cheatsheet lives in docs/cheatsheets for quick reference.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash merge by Priya Shah on 2026-02-01. Changelog: documented in release_notes and top-level README updated to link the quickstart. Rollout: immediate; flagged on the docs site sidebar under "Authoring & Quickstarts".

Notes for maintainers: Keep the wasm adapter small — it exists to simulate tool behaviors rather than be production adapter code. If we later expand to real connectors, move under examples/connector-adapters and add explicit security review. Related tickets: ENG-1429 (authoring upgrade), PM-78 (docs prioritization), SUP-221 (customer asks for local debug tooling).
